parts.title: My first fossil
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was eight, my grandfather took me to a beach in the south of England, where he had found fossils as a boy. "Look carefully at the stones," he said. "Sometimes, an animal that lived millions of years ago is hiding in one of them."

I spent two hours walking along the beach with my head down. I found shells, old glass and a lot of grey pebbles, but nothing special. I was about to give up when something shiny caught my eye. It was a round stone with a beautiful spiral pattern on it.

"That is an ammonite," my grandfather said with a big smile. "It is about a hundred and fifty million years old." I could not believe that I was holding something that old. It was no bigger than my hand, but it felt like treasure.

I kept the fossil on my desk for years. Now, I am studying geology at university, and my grandfather is very proud. Last week, I gave him a gift: a small box with a new ammonite inside. He put it on the shelf next to his old photographs.

parts.title: The king of the dinosaurs
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Tyrannosaurus rex, often called T. rex, is probably the most famous dinosaur of all. [1] It lived about sixty-seven million years ago, in the area that is now North America.

T. rex was about twelve metres long and as heavy as an African elephant. [2] Its head alone was over a metre and a half long, and its teeth were as long as bananas.

For a long time, people thought that T. rex was a slow animal. [3] Scientists now believe that it could probably walk quickly but could not run very fast.

The arms of T. rex were very short, and they could not even reach its mouth. [4] They were strong, however, and may have helped the animal to hold its food.

The first almost complete skeleton was found in 1902. [5] Today, you can see a copy of it in museums all over the world.
sentences: Its bones were found in rocks in places such as Canada and the United States.
It was sold to a museum for a large amount of money.
This is why children everywhere love to draw and read about it.
New studies show that this idea may not be correct.
Some of them were over forty metres long.
Plants also grew much taller than they do today.
It had a huge head with a very powerful bite.
For many years, scientists did not know what they were for.

gaps.explanation: The sentence about bones found in Canada and the United States follows the place where it lived.
A huge head with a powerful bite follows the animal's size, and the next sentence gives the head's length.
New studies show the idea of a slow animal may be wrong, so scientists now believe it could walk quickly.
Scientists did not know what the short arms were for, and the next sentence says they were strong.
The skeleton sold to a museum explains why a copy can be seen in museums today.

parts.title: Why did the dinosaurs disappear?
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: About sixty-six million years ago, something terrible happened to the Earth. A giant rock from space, [1] than ten kilometres wide, hit the ocean near Mexico. The hit sent so [2] dust and smoke into the air that the sky went dark. Plants could not grow in the cold and dark, and animals [3] ate the plants soon had no food. Slowly, most of the big dinosaurs died out. However, some small dinosaurs [4] able to survive, and we know them today as birds. [5] you look at a bird in your garden, you are looking at a very distant relative of T. rex. It is a surprising thought, [6] it is true.

gaps.explanation: More than ten kilometres: comparative form for size.
So much dust and smoke: an uncountable quantity.
Animals that ate the plants: a relative pronoun.
Some small dinosaurs were able to survive: plural past.
If you look at a bird: a condition for the idea.
It is a surprising thought, but it is true: contrast.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Welcome to the dinosaur hall, everybody. Let me start by asking you to think about how big the dinosaurs were. Many children think they were as small as a horse, three metres long, like the little one next to the door, but that was a baby. The famous T-rex was about twelve metres, as long as a bus, and it is the one that everybody remembers. But the real giants were the plant-eaters. This skeleton behind me, with its long neck, was more than thirty metres from nose to tail, longer than two buses. Please stay behind the rope.

question.prompt: How long were the biggest dinosaurs?
question.explanation: Three metres is a baby and twelve metres is the tyrannosaurus; the long-necked giant behind the guide was more than thirty metres.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Hi, it’s Atticus. I’m standing at the museum entrance and the girl at the desk says I need my ticket to go in. I thought I had left it in the museum shop yesterday, when I bought that postcard, so I phoned them, but they haven’t got it. I also searched the bus seat, and the driver said nobody handed anything in. I think I know now. When I was making coffee this morning, I put it down beside the cups in the kitchen, and then I left in a hurry. Could you bring it to me, please. Hurry up!

parts.title: A talk about fossils
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: marguerite
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to our fossil workshop. A fossil is the remains of a plant or an animal that lived a very long time ago. Most fossils are found in a type of rock which is called limestone. You will also find some in sandstone, but limestone is the best for the type of fossils that we can look for here. How does a fossil form? Let me explain. When an animal dies in water, its body goes down to the bottom. The mud covers it. Over millions of years, more mud arrives on top, and the pressure is very strong. The mud slowly becomes stone. The bones are inside, and they are not lost. Soft parts are different. Skin and muscles are not strong, so in most cases they disappeared completely over time. We rarely find them. Many people think that the largest fossil ever found was a dinosaur, but I read that it was a tree. It was a giant tree, and it was so long that they could not move it. Today, you will not find anything that big. Let me give you a few rules for the afternoon. First, safety. The cliffs are high and stones can fall, so you must wear a hard hat. I will give you one. You do not need boots, ordinary shoes are fine. Second, take care of what you find. Take a notebook and write down where you found each fossil, and the date. Some of you have a camera, and that is good for photographs, but the notebook is what scientists use. Without that information, a fossil is only a stone. I hope you have a great afternoon, and don’t forget to ask me questions.

gaps.prompt: Most fossils are found in a type of rock called ___
gaps.explanation: Sandstone has some fossils too, but limestone is the best here.

gaps.prompt: After millions of years the mud turns into ___
gaps.explanation: The mud slowly becomes stone because of the pressure.

gaps.prompt: Soft parts like skin usually ___ over time
gaps.explanation: Skin and muscles are not strong, so they usually disappear.

gaps.prompt: The biggest fossil that was ever found came from a ___
gaps.explanation: Many people think it was a dinosaur, but it was a giant tree.

gaps.prompt: Visitors must put on a hard ___ because of the cliffs
gaps.explanation: The cliffs are high and stones can fall, so a hard hat is needed; ordinary shoes are fine.

gaps.prompt: The place and date of each find go in a ___
gaps.explanation: A camera is good, but scientists use a notebook to write where and when.

parts.title: An interview with a fossil collector
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Atticus, you have a famous collection of fossils. How did it start?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: It started when I was ten. I didn’t go to a big museum, we lived far from one, and I hadn’t read a book about dinosaurs yet. I was playing on the beach and I found a little shell in a stone. It was like magic. I took it home in my pocket, and I still have it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Where do you keep your best pieces?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: You’d think they are in boxes in the garage, and that’s where the rubbish is. The ones I love are in glass cases in my living room, with a lamp above each. My wife says it’s like living in a museum. And no, the museum doesn’t have a room for me, though they have asked me many times.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You have a favourite, a fish. Why?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: It’s not the most expensive, I got it for a very small price in a market, and it’s not the largest either. It’s the details. You can see every bone, even the tiny ones in the tail, and the scales. It’s as if it swam yesterday. That’s what makes me happy when I look at it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You had an accident once. What did you learn?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I was digging in a cliff, on my own, and the ground fell. I broke my leg and waited for three hours until somebody came. I bought stronger tools after that, but the tools didn’t matter. Nor do I avoid cliffs, I’d miss them too much. The lesson was never to go alone. Now I always have a friend with a phone.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do with your fossils?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I don’t sell them to museums, it would feel wrong. And I give some away to friends, but only the common ones. The real joy is lending to local schools. The children touch them, ask questions, and some of them become scientists. That’s why I do it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What would you say to a beginner?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Join a club. The members will teach you, show you the best places and tell you what you have found, so you learn in months, not years. Don’t buy fossils in a shop, because that is not the same as finding them, and you don’t need to travel abroad. There are fossils near almost every town.
